name: Tryphosa
overview: Tryphosa is a female believer recognized in the New Testament as a diligent worker in the Lord. She is commended by the Apostle Paul in his epistle to the Romans, highlighting her faithful service in the early Christian community. Beyond her role as a servant of Christ, no additional personal details or tribal affiliations are recorded in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Tryphosa appears once in Scripture without a given meaning or divine origin noted. It is simply presented as a proper name in Romans 16:12, identifying this faithful woman among the early Christians.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Tryphosa beyond her mention as a fellow laborer in the Lord. There are no known relatives or connections listed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Tryphosa's significance lies in her example as a committed Christian worker during the formative years of the Church. Paul's greeting to her in Romans 16:12 serves to honor her dedication and encourages believers to follow her faithful service. Her mention, though brief, underscores the vital role women played in supporting and advancing the gospel.
